body.statement: Can one establish, uniformly over triangular arrays in \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\) with \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\), a first-order influence expansion and Gaussian approximation for the cumulant-SVD estimator that includes the same-sample estimated-\(A\) correction, remains valid when the influence covariance is singular, and yields asymptotically calibrated singularity-robust Anderson--Rubin inversion?
body.justification: This is the principal open proof boundary between conservative rate-optimal inversion and a sharp limit law with calibrated critical values.
body.gap: Long et al. treat regular environmental GMM, Andrews and Guggenberger treat supplied singular moments, and Davis--Kahan perturbation theory controls projector stability; none derives a uniform cumulant U-statistic expansion through a same-sample estimated spectral projector.
body.consumer: A solution gives practitioners efficient calibrated confidence sets when the flag is weak and the projected moment covariance loses rank.
